results.title: Creality's Pika Puts a Dual-Mode Laser/NIR 3D Scanner in Your Pocket — With Gaussian Splatting Soon - Hackster.io
highlights:
s Pika Puts a Dual
...
Creality has opened orders for a compact handheld marker-free 3D scanner, offering some impressive features at a pocket-friendly price: the Creality Pika.
...
"Pika turns real objects into editable 3D models, so every scan can move beyond capture and into creation," the company says of its latest launch. "You can refine your model, use it for 3D creation and creative reuse, and export it as STL/OBJ/PLY/ASC files to share with friends and creative communities. [The] seven parallel blue laser [scanning mode] supports detail capture up to 110,000 lux [ambient brightness] while NIR [Near Infrared] structured light with a filter reduces bright-light interference up to 80,000 lux for more stable scans."
...
Creality aims to let you capture 3D objects wherever you go, with the pocket-friendly sub-$700 dual-mode Pika 3D scanner. (📹: Creality)
...
The company has also promised a third mode to follow: Gaussian splatting, which allows multiple two-dimensional images of the same subject to be converted into a photorealistic 3D representation. Once available, in an as-yet unscheduled software and/or firmware update, the feature will provide more realistic color capture and mapping than the built-in and automated 2D-mapping functions available at launch.
...
The Creality Pika is now available to pre-order direct from the company ahead of shipping scheduled to begin later this month, with a 10% "early bird" discount putting the gadget at $629 from a planned $699 retail price; the bundle includes the scanner, two rechargeable batteries, tripod, turntable, six marker towers, 20 reflective makers, a glass calibration board, two NIR filters, USB cable, lanyard, and cleaning cloth.

results.title: Creality’s Pika Wants To Make 3D Scanning Feel As Easy As Taking A Photo
results.author: Brendan Frye
highlights:
3D scanning has long been a tedious endeavour, with even simpler options on the market feeling like they require users to learn a complex new skill. Creality is looking to change that with its new Pika portable 3D scanner.
...
Designed for portability, the Creality Pika resembles a standard point-and-shoot camera more than the complex equipment many users are accustomed to. It appears to be a major step forward for makers, creators and anyone interested in
...
printing or modelling.
...
The Pika launched July 22 for $699 USD, with a 10% introductory discount available for 20 days. It includes Wi-Fi 6 and USB 3.0 connectivity, along with two removable 3,350 mAh batteries.

results.title: Creality submits for an IPO, adds a mysterious 3D printing model website | Tom's Hardware
results.author: Denise Bertacchi
highlights:
# Creality submits for an IPO, adds a mysterious 3D printing model website
...
[Denise Bertacchi](https://www.tomshardware.com/author/denise-bertacchi)
Published
28 August 2025
...
While researching Creality’s bid to become a publicly listed company, a mysterious new e-commerce site surfaces.
...
Creality is set to become a publicly listed company on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, making it the first manufacturer of consumer-grade 3D printers to make the leap into the big time.
...
Further into the document, Creality states one of its assets is a new website we haven’t heard of called “[Nexbie](https://www.nexbie.com/).” The site is an e-commerce platform to sell physical prints. When I first found the site, it claimed to be powered by “AIGC” which stands for AI generated content. It was also full of questionably sourced 3D models with photos clearly copied from other websites.
...
I then contacted Creality to learn more about the new site, and was told the website was still in its testing phase and I had stumbled upon content that should not have been made public. The next day, the site had been refreshed, and credit had been given to the designers. All the models now say they are “out of stock.”
...
“It is positioned as an overseas e-commerce platform launched by Creality, which builds a symbiotic and mutually beneficial 3D creative ecosystem,” Ma said. “In addition, it is pioneering a replicable path towards decentralized supply chains, low-carbon production and cultural diversity. We believe Nexbie has the potential to become a paradigm case of a platform that delivers both economic and social value.”

results.title: Creality K2 Pro Launches With AI Cameras and 16-Color Printing
results.author: Varvara Koneva
highlights:
Creality K2 Pro Launches With AI Cameras and 16-Color Printing
...
August 22, 2025
...
# K2 Pro launches on Monday with AI cameras, heated chamber, and 16-Color Printing
...
Creality has officially announced the release of its latest flagship 3D printer, the K2 Pro. Priced at just $1,200 and launching on August 25, the machine boasts a blend of AI features, multicolor capabilities, and an actively heated chamber. Looks like the much-hyped Creality invention aims to position itself as the future of consumer 3D printing.
...
Additionally, the printer’s highlights include smart auto-leveling, targeting only the necessary areas of the build plate, and support for Creality Cloud, with a premium subscription for one year, bundled for early buyers. Orders between August 24 and September 24 also come with extra perks, including a two-year warranty, exclusive merchandise, and – a bit of fun! – a Creality T-shirt, while supplies last.Creality will demo the K2 Pro during a special launch livestream, giving their loyal 3D printing community its first in-depth look at what could be the company’s most innovative printer to date.

results.title: Creality Reveals New KliTek Details Ahead of the Fall 2026 Launch « Fabbaloo
results.author: Kerry Stevenson
highlights:
Creality Reveals New KliTek Details Ahead of the Fall 2026 Launch « Fabbaloo
...
KliTek toolhead [Source: Creality]
...
Creality revealed more information about their upcoming KliTek technology.
...
KliTek is Creality’s answer to tool changers, INDX, Vortek, and other methods of enabling waste-free FFF 3D printing. Waste-free solutions are clearly the future, as 3D printer operators have discovered that current filament swapping systems can waste massive amounts of material when changing colors.
...
At the time of the announcement, Creality said that the technology would be available this fall, likely in their upcoming K3 system. We didn’t know much more, but then Creality did a Q&A session on Reddit, where they revealed more details about the system.
